questions.secondaryClassification: Stimulus-based math and computer science reasoning
questions.stem:
A function approaches the same finite value from both sides of x=a, but f(a) is undefined.

Which statement most accurately explains the relevant course concept?

options.A: The concept is correctly explained because no definition can make the function continuous.
options.B: The concept is correctly explained because defining f(a) to equal the limit creates a removable continuous extension.
options.C: The concept is correctly explained because the limit must be infinite.
options.D: The concept is correctly explained because continuity depends only on the derivative at a.

questions.explanation: A removable discontinuity is repaired by matching the function value to the limit.

questions.secondaryClassification: Stimulus-based math and computer science reasoning
questions.stem:
A particle's acceleration and velocity have opposite signs on an interval.

Which statement most accurately explains the relevant course concept?

options.A: The concept is correctly explained because the particle's speed decreases on that interval.
options.B: The concept is correctly explained because the particle must move in the positive direction.

questions.secondaryClassification: Stimulus-based math and computer science reasoning
questions.stem:
A logistic model satisfies dP/dt=kP(1-P/K).

Which statement most accurately explains the relevant course concept?

options.A: The concept is correctly explained because growth is constant for all P.
options.B: The concept is correctly explained because p=K is an unstable point with positive growth.

questions.secondaryClassification: Stimulus-based math and computer science reasoning
questions.stem:
A velocity function v(t) is differentiable.

Which statement most accurately explains the relevant course concept?

options.A: The concept is correctly explained because acceleration is v'(t), and speed increases when v and v' have the same sign.
options.B: The concept is correctly explained because acceleration is the integral of velocity only.
options.C: The concept is correctly explained because speed increases whenever v' is positive, regardless of v.
options.D: The concept is correctly explained because speed is the signed value of velocity.

questions.explanation: Speed is |v|, so its change depends on the signs of velocity and acceleration.
